title: Bounds for Pure Disjoint $(r,δ)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes
abstract: We study pure disjoint $(r,δ)$-quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) without assuming a stabilizer structure. We formulate local Knill--Laflamme conditions for recovery from up to $δ-1$ erasures within a recovery block, and introduce blockwise Shor--Laflamme and unitary weight enumerators that capture how error weight is distributed across recovery sets. We establish several properties of these enumerators and use them to derive a Singleton-like bound that strengthens the known bound for disjoint $(r,δ)$-qLRCs under a purity assumption, as well as a linear-programming upper bound on the code dimension. These results provide a non-stabilizer, weight-enumerator-based approach to the study of pure disjoint $(r,δ)$-qLRCs.
summary: This paper develops advanced mathematical tools—specifically blockwise weight enumerators and linear programming bounds—to establish tighter constraints on the existence and dimension of pure disjoint quantum locally recoverable codes. By avoiding assumptions about stabilizer structure, it significantly expands the theoretical understanding of quantum error correction capabilities.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving rigorous upper bounds for pure disjoint $(r, \delta)$-Quantum Locally Recoverable Codes (qLRCs) without relying on the assumption that the code possesses a stabilizer structure.
main_result: The authors establish a new Singleton-like bound and derive linear-programming upper bounds on the code dimension, which strengthen existing results for these quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The methodology involves formulating local Knill–Laflamme conditions and introducing blockwise Shor–Laflamme and unitary weight enumerators. These enumerators are then analyzed using Linear Programming (LP) techniques.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum error correction codes defined by projectors acting on a tensor product Hilbert space, specifically focusing on the structure of local recovery operations across disjoint blocks of physical qudits.
key_observables: Blockwise Shor–Laflamme weight enumerators ($	ext{ASL}_i, 	ext{BSL}_i$) and blockwise Unitary weight enumerators ($	ext{AU}_S, 	ext{BU}_S$).
important_parameters: Code parameters include total length $n$, dimension $K$, minimum distance $d$, and local recovery parameter $\delta$.
main_assumptions: The strongest bounds are derived under the assumption that the code is 'pure' (i.e., certain weight enumerators vanish for non-zero error patterns).
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining local recovery conditions to introducing blockwise weight enumerators, proving properties of these enumerators (like $	ext{ASL}_i = K 	ext{BSL}_i$), and culminating in the derivation of the Singleton-like bound via LP methods.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, non-stabilizer techniques to constrain the parameters of quantum error-correcting codes, which is fundamental knowledge for designing robust quantum computation protocols.
